# Team working agreement

**Status:** Draft for the team to review and agree on.
**Agreed on:** _Complete together if and when the team adopts this agreement._

This lightweight agreement is intended for the Hope, Inc. ERP team. It is a
proposal, not a record that the team followed a particular process or cadence.
The team should adjust it to fit its actual availability and course
requirements.

## Collaboration

- Communicate respectfully and assume good intent.
- Keep project updates factual: distinguish completed work, work in progress,
  plans, and blockers.
- Share relevant context in the issue or pull request so teammates can
  understand and review the change.
- Ask for help early when blocked; identify the help needed rather than silently
  waiting.
- Raise disagreements about scope, safety, or acceptance criteria before
  merging, and record the agreed decision where the team can find it.

## Work and review

- Prefer a focused issue and a short-lived branch for each change.
- Before starting, agree on the intended outcome and observable acceptance
  criteria. If the task is exploratory, say so.
- Open a pull request with a summary and truthful test evidence. Do not claim a
  test, review, meeting, or sprint activity that did not happen.
- Request a teammate review when available. Resolve or explain review
  conversations before merging.
- Avoid committing credentials, service-role keys, real customer or employee
  data, or sensitive screenshots.
- For database, access-control, or destructive changes, document the security
  impact and test plan; use an approved non-production environment.

## Check-ins and impediments

The team may use the check-in template in
[check-in-and-impediment-log-template.md](./check-in-and-impediment-log-template.md)
when it actually holds a check-in. Record the date, attendees, decisions,
blocker owner, and next step. Do not backfill fictional meeting notes.

## Review and updates

The team should revisit this agreement if its availability, responsibilities, or
working approach changes. A lightweight process that the team actually uses is
more useful than a detailed plan that does not match reality.
